name: Hypertension due to gain-of-function mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor

criteria.description: Persistent elevated blood pressure consistent with hypertension
Identification of gain-of-function mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (NR3C2)
Suppressed plasma renin activity with normal or elevated aldosterone levels
Presence of hypokalemia without other identifiable causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent hypertension plus genetic confirmation of a gain-of-function mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes of hypertension and confirmation by molecular genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Hypertension refractory to standard antihypertensive therapy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypokalemia due to renal potassium wasting
pathognomonic.notes: Low serum potassium levels despite normal intake

common.notes: Proximal muscle weakness is frequently reported
searchTerms: muscle weakness due to low potassium

common.notes: Increased nighttime urination due to altered renal sodium handling

common.symptomName: Headache associated with elevated blood pressure
searchTerms: head pain linked to elevated BP

common.notes: Resulting from increased mineralocorticoid receptor activity

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to low potassium

occasional.notes: Increased urine output due to altered sodium and water handling

rare.notes: Rare severe complication of uncontrolled hypertension

rare.symptomName: Retinal vascular changes due to hypertension
searchTerms: blood vessel changes in retina from high BP
heart muscle disease from long-term high BP

laboratory: Normal to elevated serum aldosterone levels
Mild metabolic alkalosis on arterial blood gas
imaging: Echocardiogram may show left ventricular hypertrophy
genetic: Identification of gain-of-function mutations in NR3C2 gene encoding mineralocorticoid receptor
other: Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias related to hypokalemia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of adrenal adenoma or hyperplasia
No activating mutations in mineralocorticoid receptor gene
Mutations in epithelial sodium channel genes (SCNN1B or SCNN1G)

redFlags: Severe, treatment-resistant hypertension in young patients
Hypokalemia unexplained by diuretics or other causes
Early onset of hypertension with family history suggestive of monogenic cause
references: Geller DS et al. Activating mineralocorticoid receptor mutation in hypertension exacerbated by pregnancy. Science. 2000.
Funder JW et al. Mineralocorticoid receptor activation and hypertension. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2016.
Orphanet: Hypertension due to gain-of-function mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor (ORPHA:88660)
